story.name: トウキョウ ひとりぐらし
story.title: The Night the Floor Moved
story.line: ブーケが はじめて じしんに あいます
story.ja: 次の土曜の夜、歯みがき中に鏡がゆれだした。はじめての地震。ブーケは歯ブラシをくわえたまま固まってしまう。10秒ほどでおさまると、アリゲッティが「大丈夫？」と様子を見に来て、麦茶をいれてくれる。翌朝は小学校で町内の防災訓練。名簿を持ったたぬきち、消火器、煙の中を歩くテント、そして地震体験車。消防のチーフに「テーブルの下に入って、脚をしっかり持って。手を離すな」と教わる。午後はアリゲッティと赤い防災リュックを作る。水、懐中電灯、ラジオ、乾パン、そして「気持ちを落ちつける」ためのあめ。リュックは紺色の傘のとなりに。

segments.en: The next Saturday night, Rosie was brushing her teeth when the bathroom mirror began to shake.
At first, she thought it was a truck. Then the ceiling light started to swing, and the water in Mochi's bowl moved like a tiny ocean.
Oh. Oh no. Is this an earthquake? This is an earthquake. Okay. Okay. What do I do? What do I do?
She stood very still, with the toothbrush in her mouth. The floor creaked. The glasses in the kitchen rattled.
After maybe ten seconds, it just stopped. The light swung a little more and was still. Outside, a dog barked once.
Her heart was pounding. Then she heard footsteps on the stairs, and a gentle knock on her door.
Rosie? It's Gayle. Are you all right, dear? I thought I'd better check on you. Was that your first one?
Yes! I just stood there. With a toothbrush. I didn't know what to do. Was that a big one?
Oh, no, that was a small one. We get those now and then. But there's a neighborhood drill tomorrow morning, at the school. Come with me.
Gayle made them both cold barley tea, and they drank it on Rosie's floor until her hands stopped shaking.
The next morning, the school playground was full of neighbors. Kids, grandparents, families with strollers. Tom Nook was there with a clipboard, of course.
Good morning, everyone! Thank you for coming! Yes, yes. Please find your name on the list. And Rosie, welcome to your very first drill!
Firefighters had set up stations all around the playground. At one, people were taking turns with a fire extinguisher on a pretend fire.
At another, there was a tent full of harmless white smoke, and you walked through it bent over low, a cloth over your mouth.
And at the far end was a truck with a little kitchen built on the back. The sign said Earthquake Experience.
The firefighter in charge was a gray wolf with a serious face and a loud voice. His name, of all things, was Chief.
All right. In this room, we make a real earthquake. When it starts, get under the table and hold on to the leg. Don't let go. Got it?
Got it. Under the table. Hold on to the leg. Don't let go. Wait. How big is big?
Big enough. Don't worry, it's safe. It's better to feel it here, with me, than for the first time at home, alone.
Rosie and Gayle sat down in the little kitchen. And then the whole room began to shake. Not a little. A lot. Like being inside a washing machine.
Rosie dove under the table and held on to the leg with both hands. Next to her, Gayle was holding on too, and somehow she was laughing.
Hold on tight, dear! Here comes the big part! Oh, my glasses! There they go!
When it stopped, Rosie crawled out. Her legs felt like noodles. Chief looked at her for a long moment. Then he gave her a thumbs-up.
Good. You stayed under. That's the most important thing. Now. Do you have an emergency bag at home?
An emergency bag? Um. I have a suitcase. And a few rice balls. Does that count?
Don't worry, I'll help you make one. Water, a flashlight, a radio, some crackers. You never know. Better safe than sorry.
That afternoon, they filled a red backpack together. Bottles of water. A flashlight. A little radio. Hard crackers that would keep for years.
Gayle also put in a pair of socks, a whistle, and a small bag of hard candy.
The candy is for your nerves. That's not official. That's just my advice.
Back home, Rosie put the red backpack by her door, next to Gayle's navy umbrella. Looking at them, she felt a little braver.
Okay, Mochi. If the floor moves again, I'm getting under the table. And you're, well, you're already in the water. You'll be fine.
That night, a train went by, and the glasses rattled a little on the shelf. Rosie opened one eye. Then she smiled, and went back to sleep.

ph.trap: チェックする ではなく、大丈夫か見に行く
手に入れた ではなく「了解」。答えも Got it.
let go＝行かせる ではなく、つかんだ手を離す
hold on は「待って」の意味もあるが、ここは文字どおり

ph.ja: 何があるかわからないから
ph.trap: あなたは知らない ではなく「万一にそなえて」
後悔するより、用心しておくほうがいい

predict.ask: つぎの はなしで、ブーケと アリゲッティは どこへ いく？
choices: To a camping store, to buy a second emergency bag.
To Mount Fuji itself, on an early morning bus.
To the neighborhood bathhouse, with Mount Fuji painted on the wall.
predict.ja: 富士山の絵がある、近所の銭湯へ。
